title: How many home EV chargers are installed in the UK each year? About 192k chargers a year, estimated step by step
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many home EV chargers are installed in the UK each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Here is a step up to practise on. Read the question, pause, and have a go at your own estimate first, even a rough one. Then walk through the answer below and compare. Your number does not need to match; your logic is what counts.
body:
The question

How many home EV chargers are installed in the UK each year?

The approach

New electric cars × share bought by people with a driveway × share who install a charger.

Say this out loud before you touch any numbers. It lets the interviewer agree with your plan, or nudge you, before you have done any work.

Step by step

  1. New fully electric cars sold in the UK per year: 400k
  2. × 60% buyers with off-street parking
  3. × 80% of those who install a home charger

That gives about 192k chargers a year.

Does it make sense?

Second-hand electric car buyers add more installs each year.

This sanity check is the step most people skip, and one of the easiest ways to impress. It shows you care whether the number is right, not just whether the sum works.

Real-world check

About 473,000 new battery electric cars were registered in the UK in 2025 (SMMT), more than the 400,000 assumed here. Rerun with that figure and you get about 230,000 home chargers, a good reminder to update an input when you learn a better one.

Source: SMMT: new car registrations, December 2025.

Your turn

Try a similar question in the free market sizing drill, which checks your logic step by step.
outro: If your estimate was far off, look for which step made the difference. That is where the learning is, and it is exactly what an interviewer would ask about.
